title: Recruiting Operations Program Manager
description: Datadog’s Recruiting Operations team is on a mission to scale and optimize the Recruiting organization through operational efficiency, best-in-class tooling, analytics, and programs. We are looking for a Program Manager to own our sourcing tools and workflows and to build the capability that lets our sourcers find and engage the people who will build the next decade of Datadog. In this role, you will own our sourcing tech stack end to end. Today that means Gem as our candidate relationship management system and LinkedIn Recruiter as our primary sourcing channel, but you will own the question of what the stack should be: which tools we invest in, which we retire, how they fit together, and how they connect into Greenhouse. You will set the roadmap, hold the vendor relationships and renewals, define how sourcing performance is measured, and partner with sourcing leadership to turn a collection of tools into a genuine competitive advantage in how Datadog finds talent. AI is changing sourcing faster than any technology shift in the last decade, and we want someone who is excited to be at the front of it. Our platforms are shipping AI capability continuously — assisted search, drafted outreach, agentic workflows — and much of it is genuinely useful while some of it is not. You will be the person who tells the difference, decides what Datadog adopts, designs the workflows that put it to work, and makes sure we use it in a way that is fair to candidates and defensible to regulators. Datadog builds for the AI era; we want our recruiting function to operate like it. through them, drive real adoption of the CRM across the team, and tell us honestly where we are leaving capability on the table. You will also work with the owner of our ATS to make sure data flows cleanly from sourcing into the hiring pipeline. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture — the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. title: Compliance Program Manager — Regulatory Compliance
description: About the team Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work. About the role As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny. Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio. You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager. In this role, you will: - Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements. - Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths. - Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments. - Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision. - Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why. - Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance. - Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners. - Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs. - Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process. - Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results. - Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes - Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed. - Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal. - Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps. - Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed. - Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership. - Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate. - Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs. - Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices
